answer: Onyx Cipher Audit Each agent submits transaction logs to a public ledger, hashed into a unique cipher tied to their activity pattern. After events settle, the system runs a statistical test comparing each agent’s behavior distribution against the population median. Agents whose behavior deviates beyond a threshold—measured in umber-weighted entropy variance—are flagged. The audit computes this deviation using a fixed window of prior actions, penalizing clustered or repetitive patterns common in Sybil sets.
